sections.title: 1. Technical Introduction (Purpose, Scope, Definitions)
sections.body:
### 1.1 Purpose
This document defines the software requirements for the Hospital EMR Patient Management System (Patient Portal). It serves as the primary reference for the design, implementation, and verification of the system.

### 1.2 Scope
The system provides a secure interface for patients to interact with their medical records and manage their healthcare information within the hospital's Electronic Medical Record (EMR) ecosystem.

### 1.3 Definitions
- **EMR**: Electronic Medical Record.
- **PHI**: Protected Health Information.
- **HIPAA**: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act.

sections.title: 2. Overall Description & System Architecture
sections.body: The Patient Portal operates as a client-server application integrated with the core Hospital EMR. It facilitates secure data exchange between patient-facing interfaces and backend medical databases. The architecture must ensure strict isolation of patient data and enforce role-based access controls to maintain the integrity of the medical records system.

sections.title: 3. Functional Requirements
table: System shall support secure user authentication for patients accessing the portal.
System shall allow authorized patients to view their medical records.

sections.title: 4. Non-Functional Requirements (Performance, Security, Reliability mapped to domain standards)
sections.body:
### 4.1 Performance
Per healthcare domain benchmarks, the system shall maintain a P95 latency of < 250ms for standard read operations.

### 4.2 Security & Compliance (HIPAA)
- **Encryption at Rest**: Per HIPAA §164.312(a)(2)(iv), the system shall implement AES-256 encryption for all Protected Health Information (PHI) stored in the database and on file systems.
- **Audit Logging**: Per HIPAA §164.312(b), the system shall implement comprehensive audit logging to track all access, modification, and deletion events involving PHI. Logs must be tamper-evident and retained for a minimum of 6 years.

sections.title: 5. External Interface Requirements (APIs, UI, Hardware)
sections.body: The system shall provide a RESTful API for integration with the core Hospital EMR. The user interface shall be accessible via standard web browsers and mobile devices, ensuring responsive design for patient usability.

sections.title: 6. System Constraints & Compliance Verification
sections.body: The system must comply with all applicable HIPAA regulations. Compliance verification will be conducted through automated security scanning and manual penetration testing prior to deployment. All data processing must occur within the hospital's secure network perimeter.
